title: Edge session guard: coordinated traffic-shift + streaming-safe failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an edge-layer guard that enables active-active traffic shifting across regions while preserving session and streaming semantics. The feature combines region-aware routing, per-session KV transfer tokens, region-local circuit breakers, and coordinated load-shedding policies to meet p99 latency and streaming-consistency SLOs during partial outages and overloaded states.
acceptance_criteria: New edge control accepts traffic-shift policy allowing gradual percentage shifts between regions with session affinity preserved for existing long-poll/stream connections
During a simulated 30% CPU saturation in region-A handling streaming channels, traffic-policy shifts 40% new-sessions to region-B while active streams continue without data-loss >0.1%

Circuit-breaker trips isolate overloaded model instances in region-A within 500ms of threshold breach and reroutes new requests according to policy; p99 for new requests in fallback region remains <350ms

Load-shedding hierarchy reduces non-critical request classes (embedding, low-priority batch) before degrading chat generation quality; shedding actions are visible in Console with per-route impact metrics
Automated rollback if cross-region streaming error-rate delta >1% for 10m during canary shift
All changes covered by integration tests (synthetic multi-region streaming harness) and load tests in staging with pass/fail artifacts linked
plan_steps: Design API for traffic-shift policy (percentage, sticky-duration, transfer-mode: cold|live-token)
Add per-session transfer token mechanism: ephemeral KV transfer IDs stored in control-plane with TTL and HMAC signing
Extend gateway to support live-token handshake to rehydrate session state on new region in-flight for streaming connections
Implement region-local circuit breakers with adaptive thresholds (latency, queue-depth, error-rate) and global coordinator to avoid flapping
Add load-shedding policy engine with prioritized buckets and graceful degradation rules (token-budget clamps, shorter horizons for streaming frames)
Instrument metrics and traces: session-transfer-success, streaming-resume-latency, circuit-breaker-trigger-count, shed-rate-by-route
Create end-to-end tests and chaos experiments (region fail, spike CPU, network partition) in staging cluster
Rollout: internal canary -> 5% customer traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automated safety gates
design_decisions: Stickiness model: first-request hashed to region for N minutes (default 10m) to reduce cross-region rehydration frequency
Session transfer: prefer live-token rehydration for active streams when possible; cold transfer (start new session + best-effort KV repopulation) used if live transfer fails
Circuit-breaker scoping: per-model-instance + per-region aggregates; global coordinator keeps a conservative recovery cooldown to avoid oscillation
Load-shedding order: background embeddings -> non-urgent batch -> lower-quality model fallback -> token-accuracy reduction (response truncation)
Observability: emit both pre- and post-shift metrics so we can compute delta and detect regressions quickly
rollout_strategy: Feature gate behind runtime-1.20 and console flag user-visible for operators
Step 0: deploy gateway + control-plane changes to staging; run synthetic streaming harness (10k concurrent sessions) until stable
Step 1: internal canary with 1% production traffic from non-critical accounts for 24h
Step 2: 5% customer traffic with progressive increase over 48h while monitoring streaming-resume-latency and session-loss-rate
Safety gates: abort if streaming-resume-latency p95 increases >20% or session-loss-rate >0.2% over baseline
Final: full roll after two business-day monitoring window and PM sign-off
risks: State transfer for live streaming is complex; risk of inconsistent KV leading to subtle user-visible content glitches
Cross-region latency may make live-token rehydration take longer than allowed SLO; fallback must be robust
Circuit-breaker misconfiguration can cause over-eager shedding and double-redirects between regions
Observability gaps could mask regressions during gradual rollouts leading to customer impact
